_comment: All pixel coordinates are expressed in REFERENCE FRAME space (see reference_size),
which matches reference.jpg. They are rescaled to the native video resolution at runtime,
and warped by the per-clip alignment transform to compensate for camera drift.
Speed comes from 'camera_model': a real pinhole camera resting on the road plane.
Every track point is mapped to feet on that plane and distance-vs-time is fitted.
The two mailbox gates are kept as an independent timing cross-check.
which draws a one-foot ground grid. It should lie flat on the asphalt.

derivation: horizon: least-squares fit to a 6'1" person standing at 8 road-surface stations
in the calibration walk (Driveway-04-181001-181152.mp4). For a constant-
height object on a plane, (y_feet - y_head) is linear in (x_feet, y_feet),
so the horizon falls straight out. Fit residual 2.6 px.
road_vanishing_point: 38 real vehicle tracks over 45 clips, each track's ground-
contact line constrained to pass through it, and it constrained to the horizon.
cross_road_vanishing_point and camera_height_ft: the only two fitted parameters,
solved against the four laser distances below. Fit rms 1.1%.
focal_px follows from the two vanishing points being orthogonal ground directions.
Stations on the elevated far lawn were excluded -- they are not on the road plane.
The driveway edges were NOT used for the cross-road direction: the driveway slopes,
so its edges do not lie in the road plane.
camera_model.axes: X runs along the road, increasing to the RIGHT on screen. Y runs across the road, away from the camera.
validation_note: None of the four distances above were used to fit the horizon or the road vanishing
point; two free parameters were fitted against them, so this is close to but not
fully independent. The 28.80 ft mailbox figure was measured inside-face to inside-face
while the model measures post base to post base, so a small positive bias is expected.
Independent check: the 24x18in sign in the calibration walk reproduces to -0.4% mean.

vanishing_point_note: Both lie on the fitted horizon, as they must. The previous values did not: they were 171 px and 320 px off it, and implied a 135-degree lens.
baseline_note: Along-road distance between the two mailbox POST BASES, derived from camera_model.
Laser tape gives 28.80 ft inside-face to inside-face of the mailboxes themselves,
which sit above and inboard of the posts, so 29.05 ft base-to-base is consistent.
Used only by the two-gate timing cross-check, not by the primary measurement.
gates_note: Regenerated from camera_model as true cross-road lines through each post base, spanning Y = -4 to 24 ft. Genuinely parallel on the ground, so the baseline holds in either lane.

_note: Laser measurements, kept for validation. These pixels are NOT used to build the
camera model -- three of them cluster in a near-vertical line and are close to
degenerate, which is what broke the previous ground_plane homography.
Pixel accuracy is known to be imperfect: street_manhole_center sits on the right
edge of the manhole rather than its centre, and driveway_left_asphalt_corner sits
slightly into the grass. Re-pick them before relying on these residuals.
survey.measurement_note: 16.92 ft driveway width; 20.07/30.57 ft from left/right corners to manhole; 20.42 ft across road at left corner.
